pain_points.description: The worktree.create example notes you must declare contract+writes for framework-provided fields. This is unusual (most engines auto-populate framework fields) and easy to miss; AUTHORING.md flags it twice but a single 'why' sentence (vs. just 'because the rule says so') would land it faster.

There is no dedicated 'commit/push' step type; you reach for a generic script step with `git add/commit/push`. The §2 note on merge_to_base ('typically created by a preceding script step that runs git add/commit/push') makes this clear, but the lack of a first-class git step means every code-mutating workflow re-implements the same shell snippet.

Branching on a check is single-direction (`on_fail: cancel`). The 'cancel on FAIL, commit on PASS by virtue of ordering' pattern works but is implicit — a reader must infer that placing commit-and-push *after* the gate is what makes the workflow correct. An explicit `on_pass`/`on_fail` pair would be more self-documenting.

Table lists `command:` as a substitution site for $state/$inputs, but a multi-line bash `command: |` with `$inputs.ticket_id` mixed alongside shell `$var` syntax invites confusion about precedence/escaping. A one-line note ('$-substitution runs before bash, so $inputs.X is replaced literally') would remove the ambiguity.

The task said 'off main' but the canonical pattern uses `base: $inputs.base_branch`. AUTHORING.md doesn't show a literal `base: main` form; I defaulted the input to `main` to stay idiomatic, but a one-line 'literal branch names are also accepted' would save a moment of doubt.

self_assessment: The workflow expresses the 4-stage shape cleanly: worktree.create -> ai/implement (writes_files, empty contract) -> ai/review + check (cancel on FAIL) -> script(commit+push) + worktree.cleanup(merge_to_base). Standard prompts fit both AI nodes via template_vars, contracts/writes are consistent, and the cancel-on-fail gate keeps the commit step from running on a failed review. Main uncertainty is whether the inline `commit -m "fix($inputs.ticket_id): ..."` substitution composes cleanly with the bash heredoc, but §4 lists `command:` as a substitution site so this should resolve at load time.
